$MU - Still Torn between Cyclical & Structural?
(Update from $MU Q4 Earnings)

8 months+ have passed since this post, and the greatest debate on whether $MU is cyclical or structural is still as hot as ever, and market is torn between valuing $MU as a structural play (this time is really different?), or just a cyclical play (fundamentals seem the best when a cyclical stock topped?). That translates to the volatilities we saw on the chart reflecting the constant tug-of-war between the buyers and sellers, between the believers and the non-believers.

A) What I Don't Know

This post is not going to tell you that $MU is 100% cyclical or structural. Conviction and cognition can't be borrowed, and you should respect your own process and do what you are comfortable with. TBH, I have my bias (that perhaps this time is structural), but ultimately, I don't have a crystal ball and I know that there is no such things as 100% certainty. 

I don't know how's the supply situation going to play out for the three memory giants (MU, SKHY, Samsung) which depends on their discipline in curbing their production ramp up. I don't know how is the demand side - how big and how long is the AI run way, and how the development and technology advancement may impact (either accelerate the demand or render some redundancy/ replacement).

My conviction is loosely held. In the context of a thematic position trader, I will try to sit on my core for as long as possible unless the fundmentals and/or trend can convince me that its uptrend is really over (which it hasn't).

B) What I Do Know 
(from earnings presentation slides)

i) MU is still firing on all cylinders

With CDBU sector, now 33% of the total revenue, leading the charge.

ii) Another sequential growth into the next quarter with a highish gross margin level of 86.25%, which the management expect to be the floor in fiscal 2027.

iii) Physical AI could be the next exciting TAM, on top of the existing AI needs for memories and storage.

iv) 26 SCAs is now estimated to be over 35% of their revenue through 2030 (of which 3/4 has defined pricing bands with floor and ceiling while the other 1/4 negotiated periodically). This enhances visibility for a few years (note: some bears might say that the price cap on this portion has sacrificed some insane upsides for stability, so we can't really please everybody!).

C) What You Should Know

I can't predict how the price will move.
Have your own plan.
Respect risk.
Have fun.

The Financial Times published an Opinion piece written by Bill Gross, yesterday.

BOTTOM LINE
Credit expansion is crucial for economic growth, but unbalanced balance sheets, particularly in government debt and AI-related investments, currently pose heightened risk.  Gross advises caution with both stocks and bonds, favoring short-term Treasury bills and only a few opportunities in income funds (each carrying its own risks).

SUMMARY
Gross argues that US credit growth, about 5.9% on roughly $84tn of total credit, is what is holding asset prices up against 8% nominal GDP growth. He sees the balance sheets behind that growth as increasingly unbalanced. Hyperscalers are borrowing hundreds of billions for data centers, and the $1Tn of AI investment forecast for 2027 will likely be funded by debt alone because positive cash flow has disappeared. 

Meanwhile, US net debt is near 100% of GDP. In his view, this buys growth now, lower growth later, and higher inflation with no relief unless global fiscal and debt markets are contained. 

His positioning is to own no bonds except one-year T-bills at 4.55%, to be cautious on record-high stocks because higher yields will compress margins.

Gross recommends avoiding hyperscalers unless their P/E is under 20. On a strict reading of his screen, only Alphabet qualifies on trailing earnings, and only Oracle on forward earnings.

He floats Verizon and AT&T for yield, though Starlink Mobile threatens them, and discounted income funds such as Nuveen Preferred & Income Opportunities (8% discount to NAV, 11% yield, but vulnerable if short rates rise.

Focusing on Relative Strength (RS) names during pullbacks is a core strategy in momentum trading because it shifts probabilities significantly in your favor. When the broader market pulls back or consolidates, how a stock reacts reveals its underlying institutional sponsorship and supply-demand dynamics.

Key Reasons to Focus on RS Names on Pullbacks

Institutional Accumulation:
 Stocks showing high relative strength don't drop easily because heavy institutional buyers (mutual funds, ETFs, pensions) are aggressively defending their positions or continuing to accumulate shares quietly rather than dumping them.

The "Spring" Effect:
When the general market corrects, weak stocks plunge aggressively. RS names tend to pull back in a controlled, orderly fashion (often on declining volume). Once the market index stabilizes or resumes its uptrend, these resilient stocks are primed to snap back and lead the next leg higher with explosive force.

Clear Risk-to-Reward Setup: 
Pullbacks in leading RS stocks offer defined technical entry points (such as moving averages, previous breakout levels, or flag patterns). This allows you to set tight, logical stop-losses just below the pullback support, maximizing your potential upside relative to your risk.

Avoiding "Value Traps":
Buying a weak stock just because it looks "cheap" or has pulled back heavily often leads to buying a falling knife. RS names are typically outperforming for fundamental reasons (such as strong earnings growth or positive guidance), meaning you are buying market leaders on sale rather than broken companies.

$RKT remains my favorite way to express a view on lower long-end rates, because unlike simply owning duration, I potentially get a second layer of upside from the underlying business.

Rocket is no longer just the mortgage company most people remember from a few years ago.

Following the Mr. Cooper and Redfin acquisitions, Rocket now services roughly $2 trillion of mortgages across ~9 million loans, giving it the largest servicing portfolio in the industry.

In Q2:

• $49.1B mortgage origination volume
• 6.2% purchase market share (record)
• 14.3% refinance market share (record)
• $766M adjusted EBITDA
• Redfin mortgage leads doubled YoY in June

That servicing book is particularly important.

If rates eventually fall, millions of existing borrowers become potential refinance candidates, and Rocket already owns the relationship with many of them.

That creates what I view as a very interesting form of operating leverage to lower rates.

My macro thinking is relatively simple.

As we approach the midterms, I believe the incentives for some form of resolution or de-escalation around Iran increase. If there is no compromise, persistent high oil prices could increasingly weigh on the economy.

And even if geopolitical conditions improve, some of the economic impact from the oil shock may continue filtering through with a lag.

There are therefore several different paths that could eventually push long-end yields lower:

-geopolitical de-escalation
-economic slowing
-falling inflation expectations
-easier monetary conditions
-policy or Treasury-market intervention.

Instead of simply owning a long-duration Treasury position, $RKT gives me exposure to that same broad rate direction while also owning a business whose earnings power could improve materially if mortgage activity normalizes.

At ~$11.65, consensus currently has RKT earning roughly:

2026: $0.62
2027: $0.86
2028: $1.05

That means I'm paying roughly:

19x 2026 EPS
13.5x 2027 EPS
11x 2028 EPS

And the forward return math gets interesting quickly.

At just 15x 2028 EPS, the stock is ~$15.70.
At 18x, ~$18.80.
At 20x, ~$20.90.

That equates to roughly 14%, 24% and 30% annualized returns respectively through the end of 2028, before considering the possibility that EPS estimates themselves rise in a materially better mortgage environment.

That last part is really the thesis.

If rates stay high, Rocket is increasingly becoming a scaled, integrated housing platform with Redfin, origination, servicing, title and personal finance.

If rates fall, I potentially get the same macro trade I wanted from duration, but with a multiplier through higher mortgage volumes, refinancing activity, recapture and earnings.

Not just a pure bond proxy.

A levered equity expression of the same macro view, attached to what I think is becoming a much better business.

One thing I've learned over the years is that you don't need an opinion on everything to be a successful trader.

Housing, inflation, yields, geopolitics... I enjoy following all of it and understanding the bigger picture, but that doesn't mean every piece of information needs to influence my trading decisions.

I've built a system around price, market internals, leadership and risk management. If something genuinely starts affecting the market, I expect that impact to eventually show up in the data I actually trade. That's when I'll react.

Otherwise, constantly introducing new information into your decision-making process is a great way to start second-guessing perfectly valid setups, developing biases and overriding your own rules.

There's a big difference between being informed and letting information dictate your trading.

Trading with a cushion:
Whether it's built-up realized gains from previous weeks or breathing room in an open position is the ultimate trading weapon because it completely alters the psychological and mathematical dynamics of execution.

Here is why having a cushion changes everything:

Eradicates Decision Fatigue and Fear: 
When you are trading from a deficit or breaking even, every tick feels like life or death. A cushion absorbs the psychological blow of normal market noise, keeping your mind clear and objective.

Allows You to Let Winners Run: 
Fear of giving back profits usually causes premature exits. When you have a comfortable cushion, you can sit through normal intraday or multi-day drawdowns without flinching, allowing asymmetric trades to fully materialize.

Frees Up Aggression on High-Conviction Setups: 
Knowing you have a buffer gives you the freedom to step up when a pristine, high-relative-strength setup appears, without the paralyzing anxiety of capital destruction.

Protects Against Choppy Tapes: 
Markets fluctuate wildly. A cushion acts as a financial shock absorber, carrying your account through messy rotations without forcing you into revenge trading.

In short, a cushion shifts your entire posture from defense to offense. It turns trading from a stressful scramble into a calm, systematic business.
